text.p: These are the leading stories in the Albanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- An editorial says President Sali Berisha is playing a bluff after the leader of his Democratic Party, Tritan Shehu, suggested early elections should be held on June 15 at a time when other parties have not agreed how they are to be held.
- Recently discovered documents show how the secret police surveyed local authorities, students and journalists during the unrest in Vlore.
- Businessmen complain of a possible new increase to 18 per cent of value-added tax from the current rate of 12 percent.

- President Berisha tells OSCE envoy Franz Vranitzky to visit southern Albania and consider whether elections can be held with the rebel committees. Prime Minister Bashkim Fino says committees are not dangerous any more and asks that multinational troops should guard polling stations.
- The European Union will provide some $11.8 million aid to Albania.
- Newspaper editorial says Franz Vranitzky found a tense political situation in Albania with a Socialist Party unprepared to face new elections and the Democratic Party ready to hold them on June 15.
- Multinational troops and their APCs have started to patrol the streets of the southern port town of Vlore.
- Vranitzky cannot resolve the problem of the elections, says a newspaper headline on the second page covering the OSCE envoy's visit.
- The draft state budget has been passed by the parliamentary economic committee but still not by parliament itself.
- Albanians, deported back from Italy which they tried to enter illegally on boats, say they were treated as criminals by Italian authorities.
